description: Whole agentic pipeline in one YAML. `source: + steps: + outputs:` — every step becomes a first-class Dagster asset with cost / latency / tokens / router-reasoning as metadata. 16 ops for the common shapes (single call, routing, debate, critique, synthesis, MCP tool calls, tool-use loops, framework handoffs, map, extract, classify, reduce, self-reflect, sub-pipelines, calls to pre-built agents). Any LiteLLM provider. Reusable `personas:` + pre-built `agents:` declared once and referenced by name.

inputs.description: Source text — literal, url, file, database, or upstream_asset (kind = literal|url|file|database|upstream_asset). Or omit and let an `mcp_call` step drive the pipeline directly. Partitioned: `{partition_key}` / `{partition.<name>}` / `{partition_start}` / `{partition_end}` are templated into literal text, file path, url and database query (database values are bound as quoted SQL literals; do not quote the placeholder). A partitioned literal source with no placeholder (and none in any step) is rejected at load; file/url/database with none log a warning (every partition would read the same input) unless `full_read_per_partition: true` says it is deliberate (file/url/database only). A `url` source also takes `headers` ({name: value}, templated) and `headers_env` ({Header-Name: ENV_VAR}, resolved at run time so tokens stay out of YAML).

outputs.description: One or more first-class asset outputs (declared via outputs.assets: [step_ids]); each is a dict `{text, ...op-specific fields}`. Plus optional text / json sinks.

asset_name_prefix.label: Asset Name Prefix
asset_name_prefix.description: Prefix for emitted asset names. Each step listed in outputs.assets becomes '{prefix}_{step_id}'.

source.label: Source
source.description: Data source. kind = literal | file | url | database | upstream_asset. All string fields are {partition_key}-templated.

steps.label: Steps
steps.description: Ordered pipeline steps. Each: {id, op, ...op-specific args}. Two wiring modes (compose per step): (1) legacy `source: <step_id>` reads that step's text into `{text}`; (2) typed `inputs: {port: {from: step_id} | {literal: value}}` — each port becomes a `{port_name}` placeholder in prompt_template / system_prompt (and, for mcp_call, in string tool_args). 18 ops available: llm_call | route | conditional_route | debate | critique_loop (optional `until_score_gte:` for adaptive termination) | synthesize | mcp_call | tool_use_loop | handoff | map (fan-out LLM per item in a list) | extract (structured JSON via output_schema) | classify (text → label from fixed set) | reduce (LLM-fold over chunks) | self_reflect (one-shot draft+critique+revised) | sub_pipeline (invoke inline sub-pipeline as one step) | agent_call (dispatch to a pre-built agent declared in the `agents:` block) | delegate (dynamic sibling of route/agent_call -- an LLM picks the best-matching agent from a DISCOVERED pool, sibling AgentCardComponent instances and/or an external agent-card manifest, instead of a fixed inline list, then invokes it over MCP or HTTP; validates MCP tool_args against the picked agent's real server-declared inputSchema before calling; pre-filters candidates by required_tags/required_capabilities/input_mode before any LLM is involved) | invoke_component (call an EXISTING component's real asset compute function directly, in-process, against this step's data -- no new asset/lineage node -- for reusing a deterministic transform already in the catalog, e.g. filter/sort/rank/unique_dedup, mid-pipeline between two agent steps). LLM ops accept `reasoning_effort` (OpenAI o1/o3 low|medium|high) and `thinking_budget` (Gemini 2.5+ / Anthropic thinking max reasoning tokens); LiteLLM `drop_params` silently drops them for non-reasoning models. `approve` steps: `approval_dir`, `key`, `summary`, `wait_seconds`, `on_timeout` (reject|approve|pending), `on_reject`, plus approval binding: `reuse` (until_changed default | once | always), `max_age_hours` (token older than this is expired), `bind_to` ([text, summary] default; what is fingerprinted). A token is honoured only if its fingerprint matches the current request; otherwise the run logs why (input changed since approval / approval expired / consumed) and requests approval again. Full per-op JSON Schema is published under manifest agent_hints.steps_schemas (discriminated union on `op`).

outputs.label: Outputs
outputs.description: Output declaration. Shape: {assets: [<step_ids>], text_sinks: [{from, path}], json_sinks: [{from, path}]}. `assets:` step outputs become first-class Dagster assets; sinks are side effects. All sink paths are `{partition_key}`-aware.

personas.label: Personas
personas.description: Named reusable LLM sub-configs. Each persona bundles `{model, api_key_env_var, api_base_env_var, system_prompt, temperature, max_tokens, reasoning_effort, thinking_budget}`. Reference from any step / sub-config via `persona: <name>`; the persona's fields are merged into the step's config (explicit inline fields ALWAYS win — persona is a defaults-provider). Reference sites: step-level (llm_call, classify, extract, reduce, self_reflect, map, tool_use_loop) and sub-configs (route.router, route.specialists[*], conditional_route.specialists[*], debate.proposers[*], debate.arbitrator, critique_loop.drafter, critique_loop.critic). Personas are inherited into sub_pipeline steps automatically.

agents.label: Agents
agents.description: Named pre-built agents dispatched by the `agent_call` op. Each entry: `{kind: openai_assistant | remote_agent | handoff, ...kind-specific fields}`. `openai_assistant` runs a thread+run against OpenAI's Assistants API (requires `assistant_id_env_var` + `api_key_env_var`). `remote_agent` makes an authenticated HTTP call to your deployed agent — sync or async (returns `status_url`, polled until terminal); supports `payload_template`, `response_text_path` (JSON path into reply), `auth_bearer_env_var` / `headers_env`, `poll_url_path` / `poll_terminal_status_path` / `poll_terminal_success` / `poll_interval_seconds` / `poll_timeout_seconds`. `handoff` invokes a Python callable via `entry_module` + `entry_callable` — for wrapping LangGraph / AutoGen / CrewAI / DSPy. Agents are inherited into sub_pipeline steps automatically.

group_name.label: Group Name
group_name.description: Group name for emitted assets. Default: 'agents'.

tags.label: Tags
tags.description: Additional tags for the emitted assets.

partition_type.label: Partition Type
partition_type.description: Partition type shared by every emitted asset. Omit for unpartitioned. Use `{partition_key}` in source text / URL / file path / sink paths to substitute per partition.

partition_start.label: Partition Start
partition_start.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) for time-based partition types (daily/weekly/monthly/hourly/multi).

partition_values.label: Partition Values
partition_values.description: Comma-separated string OR list — the fixed partition keys for static/multi partitioning. e.g. ['NVDA', 'TSLA', 'META'] or 'NVDA,TSLA,META'.

dynamic_partition_name.label: Dynamic Partition Name
dynamic_partition_name.description: Name for the DynamicPartitionsDefinition when partition_type='dynamic'.

partition_dimensions.label: Partition Dimensions
partition_dimensions.description: Multi-axis partition spec: list of {name, type, start, values, dynamic_partition_name}. Set INSTEAD of partition_type for multi-dimensional partitioning.

per_step_ops.label: Per-Step Ops
per_step_ops.description: When true, emit as @dg.graph_multi_asset with ONE OP PER STEP instead of a single @multi_asset. Runs page shows N step_keys (`{prefix}_ingest`, `{prefix}_{step_id}` per step, `{prefix}_extract`) instead of one composite op. Native per-op retry via Dagster's re-execution machinery — restart from any failed step. State dict serializes through the IO manager between ops. Default false keeps zero-overhead single-op behavior for high-throughput pipelines.

partition_key_parser.label: Partition Key Parser
partition_key_parser.description: Optional template that inverts composite dynamic partition keys into named fields. e.g. `{owner}/{repo}#{issue_number:int}` — parses `dagster-io/dagster#30000` back into `partition.owner='dagster-io'`, `partition.repo='dagster'`, `partition.issue_number=30000`. Fields are then available as `{partition.<name>}` substitutions in tool_args, prompt_template, system_prompt, source.text, and sink paths. Optional `:int` / `:float` / `:bool` type suffixes preserve types when the substitution target is a pure single-placeholder value (needed for MCP tools that reject string types like GitHub's `get_issue.issue_number`). Pair with `PartitionedAssetLauncherJobComponent` for the config-driven-partition-key pattern.

backfill_policy.label: Backfill Policy
backfill_policy.description: 'multi_run' launches one run per partition, the only shape this pipeline supports: each run resolves {partition_key}, sink paths and approval keys for exactly one partition. 'single_run' is rejected at load time because one run covering a partition range has no single partition_key. Leave empty for Dagster's default (one run per partition). Ignored when no partitioning is set.

backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.label: Backfill Max Partitions Per Run
backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.description: For Backfill Policy = 'multi_run' only. Must be empty or 1: a run with several partitions has no single partition_key.

policy.label: Policy
policy.description: Guardrails on what this pipeline will do on the agent's behalf; omitted = no restrictions. Sections (all optional): `on_violation: fail|warn` (default fail); `env.allow: [NAME, 'PREFIX_*']` (env vars the pipeline may read, and the ONLY ones -- plus a minimal PATH/HOME baseline -- handed to MCP stdio subprocesses); `filesystem.read` / `filesystem.write: [paths]` (allowed roots for file sources and text/json sinks); `network.allow_hosts: [host, '*.corp.com']` (sources, MCP http/sse servers, remote agents, LLM api_base); `tools.allow` / `tools.deny: [patterns]` (the model is only shown permitted tools), `tools.max_calls_per_run: N`, `tools.arg_rules: [{tool, arg, under\|hosts\|allow_regex\|deny_regex}]` (refuse calls whose arguments leave the sandbox: e.g. a path outside ./data); `components.allow: [ClassName]` (invoke_component targets); `budget.max_cost_usd\|max_tokens\|max_llm_calls\|max_seconds` (per run) and, with `budget.ledger: {dir, compact_after_days}`, cross-run caps `max_cost_usd_per_day\|max_tokens_per_day\|max_cost_usd_per_partition\|max_cost_usd_per_month`, `budget.breaker: {trip_after_violations, cool_down_minutes, window_minutes}` and `budget.on_unknown_cost: warn\|fail`. Denied tool calls are returned to the model as an error so it can adapt; other violations raise PolicyViolation (or just log under on_violation: warn). Violations and usage are recorded as step metadata. NOTE: this is enforcement at the component boundary, not an OS sandbox -- an MCP stdio server still runs with the worker's OS permissions.

receipts.label: Receipts
receipts.description: Optional closed-loop generation receipts. `{resource_key (required: a registered ContextReceiptStoreComponent resource), caller_id, policy_version, fail_on_error (default false), outcome_signals}`. Records ONE receipt per pipeline run (per partition): a synthetic item whose source_code_version is the pipeline's prompt version (the experimented steps' version while an experiment is active), purpose 'generation' or 'experiment:<name>:<variant>'. The id is emitted as asset metadata `receipt_id` and is available as `{receipt_id}` in text_sinks / json_sinks paths (json sinks also get a `receipt_id` field), so downstream feedback (receipt_outcome_ingestion mapping.receipt_id) can attach real outcomes. `outcome_signals` (opt-in; true or {approve: {approved: 0.5, rejected: -0.7, timeout: null}, verify: {pass: 0.5, fail: -0.7}, eval: {min, max}}) records approve / verify / eval results as outcomes on that receipt (outcome_ref `auto:<step>:<kind>`; eval is scaled from min..max, default 1..scale, to [-1, 1]). A failed write never fails the run unless fail_on_error. Omit for unchanged behaviour.

experiments.label: Experiments
experiments.description: Optional A/B experiment (one at a time): `[{name, steps: [step ids], variants: {<label>: {<step id>: {model | prompt_template | system_prompt (or system) | temperature | persona | version | max_tokens | api_key_env_var | api_base_env_var}}}, fraction (0,1], seed (default 0), unit: partition|run (default partition when partitioned), min_outcomes, margin, window_days, resamples, confidence, bootstrap_seed, promote_when: {confidence, min_outcomes}, max_samples}]`. Control = the base config. Each unit (partition or run) is assigned to control or the candidate by a pure function of (seed, name, unit key), so a partition always gets the same variant; the candidate's overrides apply only to the named steps. With `receipts:` the receipt records the variant's effective prompt version and the WARN check `experiment_verdict` compares the two by real outcomes (bootstrap interval; reports ready_to_promote, never promotes). Asset code_version is unchanged by an experiment.

partition_cron_schedule.label: Partition Cron Schedule
partition_cron_schedule.description: Required when partition_type='cron'. A cron expression restricting the date axis to a custom cadence, e.g. '0 0 * * 1-5' for weekdays only (business-day cadence). Built on Dagster's TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition(cron_schedule=...).

partition_cron_fmt.label: Partition Cron Fmt
partition_cron_fmt.description: strftime format for partition keys produced by partition_type='cron'. Only change this for a sub-daily cron_schedule.
